message.text: `StateTree.size` passes every listed entry to `#sizes`, which sends each distinct readable OID to `cat-file --batch-check`. It never checks the entry count against `entryLimit` first. The base store bounds the memory for sizes with the entry limit: the decision's table says "One line per distinct readable blob, so the entry limit bounds it", and the entry limit is "checked before any size is read". `#measure` (line 310) and `retire`'s folder judgement (base line 264) both refuse before they ask for sizes. `size()` is built to answer on a tip past a limit, so on such a tip the only thing bounding the sizes lookup is the 64 MiB listing limit. That limit allows about 13 to 16 times as many entries.

evidence.snippet:
| Memory for the entries | 65,536 entries, `entryLimit`, checked before any size is read | `store.test.ts`, "the entries a tip may hold" |
| Memory for the listing of entries | 64 MiB, `listingLimit`, a KiB a line on average; git is stopped there, so the list never grows past it | `store.test.ts`, at the cap and one byte past it |
| A tip past either limit | No write of Melian's makes one: a write measures its commit by both limits before it pushes, and again after it rebuilds on a moved tip, and fails as `unreachable`, pushing nothing, when the commit would pass one. Dispose only shrinks the tip, so it works at either limit. A tip past a limit by another route still fails every call, dispose included. A writer on an older build or a push by hand can make one. A writer clears it by hand, removing files such as a changeset's folder in a commit of their own | `store.test.ts`, "the entries a write may leave" and "the bytes a tip may hold" |
| Memory for the sizes | One line per distinct readable blob, so the entry limit bounds it | the entry limit's tests |

A commit that passes is pushed whatever the tip's totals. A retirement reads only the top level of `changesets/` and the folders it was asked to retire, so it works on a tip past any limit, and it is the one call that does. A commit that fails is refused as `unreachable`, and nothing is pushed. Every other write keeps its limit checks.

explanation.what: `StateTree.size` passes every listed entry to `#sizes`, which sends each distinct readable OID to `cat-file --batch-check`. It never checks the entry count against `entryLimit` first. The base store bounds the memory for sizes with the entry limit: the decision's table says "One line per distinct readable blob, so the entry limit bounds it", and the entry limit is "checked before any size is read". `#measure` (line 310) and `retire`'s folder judgement (base line 264) both refuse before they ask for sizes. `size()` is built to answer on a tip past a limit, so on such a tip the only thing bounding the sizes lookup is the 64 MiB listing limit. That limit allows about 13 to 16 times as many entries.
explanation.whatToDo: In `StateTree.size`, when `listing.entries.length > entryLimit`, return a size that reports the entries and listing bytes and leaves record bytes uncounted (or marks them past limit), without calling `#sizes`. Alternatively, ask `cat-file` for sizes in chunks and keep only a running total, so memory stays within what the entry limit allows.
explanation.whyHere: The entry limit exists because a call holds every entry and its size in memory. This change adds a call that runs on exactly the tips that limit refuses, and in that case it holds an unbounded `cat-file` stdin string, an unbounded stdout string (`#succeed` passes no `maxBytes`) and a Map with one row per blob. The same code runs in `melian doctor`, on a developer's machine, and in `melian records size`. The head guideline was edited to say size() counts "as a read counts them before it reads a blob". The base read counts entries and refuses before it reads sizes, so it does not.

properties.failureScenario: A writer pushes a commit to `melian/state` by hand, or a host's write races past the limit. The tip holds about 850,000 entries of the form `changesets/<pr>/<a>/<b>/<n>.json`, each a distinct small blob. Each `ls-tree -r -z` line is about 75 bytes, so the listing is about 63 MiB, under `listingLimit`, and `listing()` returns every entry. `#measure` refuses this tip at line 310 before any size is read. `StateTree.size` instead calls `#sizes` on all 850,000 entries. `repository.sizes` builds a ~35 MB stdin string, collects a ~42 MB stdout string with no `maxBytes`, splits it into 850,000 strings and fills an 850,000-row Map. That is about 13 times the sizes memory the entry limit was set to allow. It happens in `melian doctor` (whose `tip size` line runs every time) and in the round workflow's `size` job, on exactly the tip where the numbers matter. The bound the decision names does not apply to this call.
